header: Photographs cannot be saved from this app (my rule: strictly not; pure helpers, no React). What a web page can and cannot do:

* CAN: refuse the browser's own ways of saving a picture: the right-click menu (Save image as, Copy image, Open image in new tab), dragging it out, the long-press menu on a phone, "Print / Save as PDF" (the pictures are not printed), and opening the picture's own address on its own (the server answers only a request that comes from a page showing the picture: `Sec-Fetch-Dest: image`).
* CANNOT: stop a screenshot, a photograph of the screen, or someone who reads the network traffic with the browser's developer tools. No website can; this keeps the casual routes shut, not those.
The browser side is src/components/ImageGuard.tsx and the rules in globals.css; the server side is src/middleware.ts (the public pictures) and the employee photo route.

doc: May this request for a picture be answered? A browser that loads a picture into a page says so (`Sec-Fetch-Dest: image`); one that was asked to OPEN the picture on its own (the address typed, "Open image in new tab", "Save link as", a download) says `document` or `empty`, and I refuse it. A request that says nothing (an old browser, a program) is not refused here: the browser side still applies, and nothing can be done against a program.

behaviours: a picture's elements are guarded: img, canvas, picture, video (any case)
so is anything inside a picture's frame (data-photo, the Enlarge button, the page of a PDF viewer); a plain paragraph or button is not
a picture loaded into a page (Sec-Fetch-Dest: image) is answered; one opened on its own (document, empty, iframe, a download) is not
a request that says nothing (an old browser, a program) is not refused by this rule
globals.css: pictures cannot be dragged, selected or long-pressed, and 'Print / Save as PDF' leaves every picture out (img, picture, canvas, video)
the root layout mounts the guard (so every page has it)
the guard refuses the right-click menu and the drag in the capture phase on the whole document, and cleans up after itself
the middleware refuses a public picture opened on its own (403, not cached) and lets a page show it
it is set to run only on picture files (not the API, not the build's own files) and on Next's image optimiser, never on pages
the employees' photograph route applies the same rule (403 to a request that opens a picture on its own; the JSON data of a picture, meta=1, is not a picture)
